building.name: North Carolina State Building Code: Building Code
building.edition: 2018 (based on the 2015 International Building Code, with state amendments)
building.local_amendments_note: No Durham amendment to the building or plumbing code was found, and state law leaves no room for one: under G.S. 143-138(e) the State Building Code applies throughout the state, and a city or county may add only a fire prevention code and floodplain rules, with the Building Code Council's approval. Durham's own Code of Ordinances (Chapter 10, Buildings and Building Regulations, on Municode) could not be opened (403), so 'no local amendments' rests on the statute, the Unified Development Ordinance and the county's department page, not on a reading of Chapter 10.
building.quote: 2.8.1. Establishment The City-County Inspections Department is authorized by the North Carolina General Statutes to enforce certain State statutes, State regulations, such as the North Carolina State Building Code, and local ordinances, including, but not limited to, ordinances related to zoning and development.
building.quote_note: The online ordinance shows pop-up definitions inside the sentence; they are left out of the quote. Sec. 2.8.4 adds that the Inspections Director 'shall be responsible for final action regarding local interpretation of matters related to the North Carolina Building Code'.
building.second_quote: The City-County Building & Safety Department provides permit, plan review, and inspection services for the City and County of Durham. These services ensure the health, safety, and welfare of the public through administration and enforcement of the North Carolina State Building Code and the zoning ordinances for both the City and County.
building.statewide_quote: (e) Effect upon Local Codes. - Except as otherwise provided in this section, the North Carolina State Building Code shall apply throughout the State, from the time of its adoption. [...] No such code or regulations, other than floodplain management regulations and those permitted by G.S. 160D-1128, shall be effective until they have been officially approved by the responsible Code Council [...]

permit.exempt_list_quote: (c) No permit issued under Article 9 of Chapter 143 of the General Statutes is required for any construction, installation, repair, replacement, or alteration costing forty thousand dollars ($40,000) or less and performed in accordance with the current edition of the North Carolina State Building Code in any single-family residence, farm building, or commercial building unless the work involves any of the following: (1) The addition, repair, or replacement of load-bearing structures. However, no permit is required for replacement of windows, doors, exterior siding, or the pickets, railings, stair treads, and decking of porches and exterior decks that otherwise meet the requirements of this subsection. (2) The addition or change in the design of plumbing. However, no permit is required for replacements otherwise meeting the requirements of this subsection that do not change size or capacity. (3) The addition, replacement, or change in the design of heating, air-conditioning, or electrical wiring, devices, appliances, or equipment, other than like-kind replacement of electrical devices and lighting fixtures. (4) The use of materials not permitted by the North Carolina State Building Code. (5) The addition of roofing, excluding replacement. (6) Any changes to which the North Carolina Fire Code applies.
permit.note: The exemption is state law (G.S. 160D-1110(c), re-read on ncleg.gov on 2026-11-24). It names commercial buildings and doesn't name toilet partitions or compartments. Whether a partition replacement is a change 'to which the North Carolina Fire Code applies' is not stated. Durham's own permit pages (durhamnc.gov) returned 403 to curl and to WebFetch and were not read. Search-result snippets, which are not evidence, show the department's page saying a building permit is 'Required for any project that includes load bearing work or any project exceeding $40K in market value' and a department FAQ on G.S. 160D-1110(c); both need a browser check. The county's page for the department says nothing on which work is exempt.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Durham job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the North Carolina rules Durham enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Durham university buildings, hospitals and clinics, research labs and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** North Carolina's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. They apply in every city in the state, and Durham's City-County Building & Safety Department enforces them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the Durham City-County Building & Safety Department issues building permits for both the city and the county. Under North Carolina law, work in a commercial building that costs $40,000 or less needs no permit unless it involves load-bearing structure, a change to the plumbing, heating, air conditioning or electrical systems, materials the building rules don't allow, new roofing or anything the fire rules cover. The list doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask the department (919-560-4144) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** North Carolina's rules call for separate men's and women's restrooms, with signs, once a space holds more than 25 people (30 for an office, 100 for a store). Where each side needs only one toilet, two single-user rooms open to anyone may be used instead, and a family restroom doesn't have to be marked for one sex. The rules in force don't provide for a shared all-gender room with several stalls, so ask the Durham City-County Building & Safety Department before planning one. State law leaves the question of who may use a multi-stall restroom to the General Assembly: state agencies, cities, counties and school boards may not set their own rules.
page.confirm_office: the Durham City-County Building & Safety Department
page.install_rule: Commercial permits in Durham come from the Durham City-County Building & Safety Department. Durham's building code sets no city contractor license. North Carolina requires a state general contractor license when the project is valued at $40,000 or more, so smaller partition jobs generally don't need one. Confirm with the North Carolina Licensing Board for General Contractors. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a project valued at $40,000 or more, the contractor needs a North Carolina general contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** North Carolina has no state law setting wages on public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded or assisted projects over $2,000. For a carpenter on building work in Durham County that rate is $19.74 an hour plus $3.63 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Durham: 4.75% state, 2.25% Durham County and 0.5% transit.
page.buyers_extra: - **Universities, hospitals and research labs:** one material and one hardware standard across many buildings, in finishes that stand up to frequent cleaning.
